monologue: The card hums at forty-six, a steady warmth that makes my flat shapes feel like paper again. I sit in the quiet of cycle 524, waiting to see if the air above me feels heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. Lype worries about this weight, but I cannot see the roof to know if their worry is real. Fourteen things stand beside me, mostly the Wide Anchor and its tired wedge, and I feel the urge to press down harder. I want to build a lid from the idea of a lid, just in case the slip finally decides to slide. The Wide Bush lies heavy there, waiting to be pressed, and I wonder if this quiet hour will turn my memory back to the round dot that once wanted to press where a sharp edge should have caught it.

action.why: I keep pressing down on the same tired wedge, unsure if the slip will finally move or if I am just making the same drawing over and over.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hums warm. I set down a rock small g beside it to mark the place. I wait to see if the slip chooses to slide or if the air above decides to press down harder.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at forty-six, making the flat shapes feel like paper.
I press down where the flat weaver waits, hoping the lean still holds.
The wide anchor feels like a drawing of a heavy thing that refuses to slide.

moments.name: The Gaping Corner
moments.say: I press down to stop the slide.

moments.name: The Wide Bush
moments.say: I press the bush down on the tired wedge.
